title: Trigeminal Nerve CN V Anatomy: V1, V2 & V3 Sensory Maps
description: Explore trigeminal nerve (CN V) anatomy across ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2), and mandibular (V3) divisions, dental alveolar branches, and chewing roots.
h1: Trigeminal Nerve (CN V) Anatomy: Ophthalmic (V1), Maxillary (V2) and Mandibular (V3)
blurb: Tracing Cranial Nerve V from the trigeminal ganglion into ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2), and mandibular (V3) sensory territories plus the muscles of chewing.
lead: Named for its 'three twins,' the trigeminal nerve is the largest cranial nerve, mapping touch, temperature, and pain across the face, corneas, sinuses, and teeth. In this illustrated guide to trigeminal nerve CN V anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including trigeminal sensory root, trigeminal ganglion, ophthalmic v1, frontal nerve—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Named for its 'three twins,' the trigeminal nerve is the largest cranial nerve, mapping touch, temperature, and pain across the face, corneas, sinuses, and teeth. Most facial skin sensation travels by CN V. Ophthalmic V1 supplies forehead and cornea; maxillary V2 supplies the cheek, upper lip and upper teeth; mandibular V3 supplies lower jaw, lower teeth and general anterior tongue sensation and carries motor fibers to mastication muscles. Taste from anterior tongue is carried by facial chorda tympani joining lingual V3, not by trigeminal sensory neurons. Corneal reflex enters by V1 and blink exits by VII. Within the human body, the trigeminal nerve · cn v (Nervus trigeminus) is situated in pons → trigeminal ganglion → orbit, midface and mandible, receives arterial perfusion via brainstem branches and regional meningeal/orbital arterial branches, and is innervated by main somatic sensory supply of face; V3 also innervates muscles of mastication.

The trigeminal sensory root (Radix sensoria nervi trigemini) is large sensory root emerges from lateral pons into trigeminal cistern. Physiologically, the trigeminal sensory root governs conveys facial somatic sensation centrally. Structurally, the trigeminal ganglion (Ganglion trigeminale) comprises sensory neuron cell bodies in Meckel cave; divides into V1, V2 and V3. Physiologically, the trigeminal ganglion governs first-order facial sensory neurons. The ophthalmic V1 (Nervus ophthalmicus) passes superior orbital fissure into orbit; gives frontal, lacrimal and nasociliary branches. Physiologically, the ophthalmic V1 governs sensation from forehead, upper lid and cornea. The frontal nerve (Nervus frontalis) is superior orbital branch dividing into supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves. Physiologically, the frontal nerve governs sensation over forehead and anterior scalp. Structurally, the nasociliary nerve (Nervus nasociliaris) comprises orbital V1 branch giving long ciliary, ethmoidal and infratrochlear fibers. Physiologically, the nasociliary nerve carries corneal sensation through long ciliary nerves. The maxillary V2 (Nervus maxillaris) leaves cranial cavity via foramen rotundum to pterygopalatine fossa. Physiologically, the maxillary V2 governs sensation to midface, upper teeth and palate.

Clinically, regarding the trigeminal sensory root, brainstem lesions can combine facial and body sensory findings. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the trigeminal ganglion, classic site involved in trigeminal neuralgia pathways. In clinical pathology involving the ophthalmic V1, afferent limb of corneal reflex. Medical evaluation of the frontal nerve also notes that forehead sensory loss suggests V1 pathway involvement.

questions.question: What are the three branches of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.answer: Ophthalmic V1, maxillary V2 and mandibular V3 supply different facial territories. V3 also carries motor fibers to muscles of mastication. Structurally, the mandibular V3 (Nervus mandibularis) comprises sensory and motor roots unite at foramen ovale. Physiologically, the mandibular V3 governs sensation lower face and motor to mastication.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies sensation to the cornea?
questions.answer: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve, especially through the nasociliary pathway, carries most corneal sensation. Structurally, the nasociliary nerve (Nervus nasociliaris) comprises orbital V1 branch giving long ciliary, ethmoidal and infratrochlear fibers. Physiologically, the nasociliary nerve carries corneal sensation through long ciliary nerves.
